# Oahu Agriculture Random Forest Classification Model
# Using spectral bands to predict agriculture land cover
# =====================================================
```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(randomForest)
library(caret)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# =======================================================
# 1. LOAD TRAINING AND TESTING DATA
# =======================================================

cat("Loading training and testing datasets...\n")

# Load the datasets you just created
train_data <- read.csv("oahu_agriculture_train_data.csv")
test_data <- read.csv("oahu_agriculture_test_data.csv")

cat("Training data dimensions:", dim(train_data), "\n")
cat("Testing data dimensions:", dim(test_data), "\n")

# Check the structure
cat("\nTraining data structure:\n")
str(train_data[, 1:10])  # Show first 10 columns

# =======================================================
# 2. DEFINE PREDICTORS AND TARGET
# =======================================================

# Define spectral bands as predictors
spectral_bands <- c("Coastal_Aerosol", "Blue", "Green", "Red", "Near_Infrared", 
                    "Shortwave_Infrared_1", "Shortwave_Infrared_2")

# Optional: Also include spectral indices
spectral_indices <- c("ndvi", "ndwi", "evi", "sr")

# Choose your predictors (start with just spectral bands)
predictors <- spectral_bands

# Target variable
target_variable <- "agriculture"

cat("Predictors:", paste(predictors, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Target variable:", target_variable, "\n")

# Ensure target is a factor
train_data[[target_variable]] <- as.factor(train_data[[target_variable]])
test_data[[target_variable]] <- as.factor(test_data[[target_variable]])

cat("Target classes:", levels(train_data[[target_variable]]), "\n")
cat("Training class distribution:\n")
print(table(train_data[[target_variable]]))

# =======================================================
# 3. PREPARE DATA FOR MODELING
# =======================================================

# Check for missing values in predictors
missing_check <- sapply(train_data[, predictors], function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
cat("\nMissing values in predictors:\n")
print(missing_check)

# Remove any rows with missing values in predictors or target
train_clean <- train_data %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.[, c(predictors, target_variable)]))

test_clean <- test_data %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.[, c(predictors, target_variable)]))

cat("Clean training data:", nrow(train_clean), "rows\n")
cat("Clean testing data:", nrow(test_clean), "rows\n")

# =======================================================
# 4. TRAIN RANDOM FOREST MODEL
# =======================================================

cat("\nTraining Random Forest model...\n")

# Create formula for the model
formula_str <- paste(target_variable, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "))
rf_formula <- as.formula(formula_str)

cat("Model formula:", formula_str, "\n")

# Train Random Forest model
start_time <- Sys.time()

rf_model <- randomForest(
  formula = rf_formula,
  data = train_clean,
  ntree = 500,                    # Number of trees
  mtry = sqrt(length(predictors)), # Number of variables at each split
  importance = TRUE,              # Calculate variable importance
  proximity = FALSE,              # Don't calculate proximity (saves memory)
  na.action = na.omit,
  do.trace = 50                   # Print progress every 50 trees
)

end_time <- Sys.time()
training_time <- end_time - start_time

cat("Training completed in", round(as.numeric(training_time), 2), "minutes\n")

# Print model summary
print(rf_model)

# =======================================================
# 5. MODEL EVALUATION ON TRAINING DATA
# =======================================================

cat("\n=== TRAINING DATA PERFORMANCE ===\n")

# Get training predictions
train_predictions <- predict(rf_model, train_clean[, predictors])

# Training confusion matrix
train_confusion <- confusionMatrix(train_predictions, train_clean[[target_variable]])
print(train_confusion)

cat("Training Accuracy:", round(train_confusion$overall["Accuracy"] * 100, 2), "%\n")

# =======================================================
# 6. MODEL EVALUATION ON TESTING DATA
# =======================================================

cat("\n=== TESTING DATA PERFORMANCE ===\n")

# Make predictions on test data
test_predictions <- predict(rf_model, test_clean[, predictors])

# Test confusion matrix
test_confusion <- confusionMatrix(test_predictions, test_clean[[target_variable]])
print(test_confusion)

cat("Testing Accuracy:", round(test_confusion$overall["Accuracy"] * 100, 2), "%\n")

# =======================================================
# 7. VARIABLE IMPORTANCE ANALYSIS
# =======================================================

cat("\n=== VARIABLE IMPORTANCE ===\n")

# Extract variable importance
importance_scores <- importance(rf_model)
print(importance_scores)

# Create importance data frame for plotting
importance_df <- data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(importance_scores),
  MeanDecreaseAccuracy = importance_scores[, "MeanDecreaseAccuracy"],
  MeanDecreaseGini = importance_scores[, "MeanDecreaseGini"]
) %>%
  arrange(desc(MeanDecreaseGini))

print("Variable importance ranking:")
print(importance_df)

# =======================================================
# 8. VISUALIZATION PLOTS
# =======================================================

# Plot 1: Variable Importance
importance_plot <- ggplot(importance_df, aes(x = reorder(Variable, MeanDecreaseGini), 
                                             y = MeanDecreaseGini)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.8) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Random Forest Variable Importance",
       subtitle = "Oahu Agriculture Classification",
       x = "Spectral Bands",
       y = "Mean Decrease in Gini") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(importance_plot)

# Plot 2: Error Rate by Number of Trees
error_plot <- data.frame(
  Trees = 1:rf_model$ntree,
  OOB_Error = rf_model$err.rate[, "OOB"],
  No_Error = rf_model$err.rate[, "No"],
  Yes_Error = rf_model$err.rate[, "Yes"]
) %>%
  reshape2::melt(id.vars = "Trees", variable.name = "Error_Type", value.name = "Error_Rate") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Trees, y = Error_Rate, color = Error_Type)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Random Forest Error Rate by Number of Trees",
       x = "Number of Trees",
       y = "Error Rate",
       color = "Error Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(error_plot)

# Plot 3: Prediction Distribution
pred_plot <- data.frame(
  Actual = test_clean[[target_variable]],
  Predicted = test_predictions
) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Actual, fill = Predicted)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(title = "Prediction Accuracy by Actual Class",
       x = "Actual Class",
       y = "Proportion",
       fill = "Predicted Class") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(pred_plot)

# =======================================================
# 9. MODEL PERFORMANCE SUMMARY
# =======================================================

cat("\n=== MODEL PERFORMANCE SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("Model Type: Random Forest\n")
cat("Number of trees:", rf_model$ntree, "\n")
cat("Variables per split (mtry):", rf_model$mtry, "\n")
cat("Training time:", round(as.numeric(training_time), 2), "minutes\n")
cat("Training samples:", nrow(train_clean), "\n")
cat("Testing samples:", nrow(test_clean), "\n")
cat("\nAccuracy Results:\n")
cat("Training Accuracy:", round(train_confusion$overall["Accuracy"] * 100, 2), "%\n")
cat("Testing Accuracy:", round(test_confusion$overall["Accuracy"] * 100, 2), "%\n")
cat("Out-of-Bag (OOB) Error:", round(rf_model$err.rate[rf_model$ntree, "OOB"] * 100, 2), "%\n")

# Calculate precision, recall, F1 for each class
test_stats <- test_confusion$byClass
if (is.matrix(test_stats)) {
  cat("\nPer-class Performance (Testing Data):\n")
  for (i in 1:nrow(test_stats)) {
    class_name <- rownames(test_stats)[i]
    precision <- round(test_stats[i, "Pos Pred Value"] * 100, 2)
    recall <- round(test_stats[i, "Sensitivity"] * 100, 2)
    f1 <- round(test_stats[i, "F1"] * 100, 2)
    cat(class_name, "- Precision:", precision, "%, Recall:", recall, "%, F1:", f1, "%\n")
  }
}

# =======================================================
# 10. SAVE MODEL AND RESULTS
# =======================================================

cat("\nSaving model and results...\n")

# Save the trained model
saveRDS(rf_model, "oahu_agriculture_rf_model.rds")
cat("Model saved as: oahu_agriculture_rf_model.rds\n")

# Save predictions
test_results <- data.frame(
  x = test_clean$x,
  y = test_clean$y,
  actual = test_clean[[target_variable]],
  predicted = test_predictions,
  correct = test_clean[[target_variable]] == test_predictions
)

write.csv(test_results, "oahu_agriculture_predictions.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Predictions saved as: oahu_agriculture_predictions.csv\n")

# Save variable importance
write.csv(importance_df, "oahu_agriculture_variable_importance.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Variable importance saved as: oahu_agriculture_variable_importance.csv\n")

# Save model performance summary
performance_summary <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Training_Accuracy", "Testing_Accuracy", "OOB_Error", "Training_Samples", 
             "Testing_Samples", "Number_of_Trees", "Variables_per_Split"),
  Value = c(train_confusion$overall["Accuracy"], 
            test_confusion$overall["Accuracy"],
            rf_model$err.rate[rf_model$ntree, "OOB"],
            nrow(train_clean),
            nrow(test_clean),
            rf_model$ntree,
            rf_model$mtry)
)

write.csv(performance_summary, "oahu_agriculture_model_performance.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Performance summary saved as: oahu_agriculture_model_performance.csv\n")

# =======================================================
# 11. HOW TO USE THE TRAINED MODEL
# =======================================================

cat("\n=== HOW TO USE YOUR TRAINED MODEL ===\n")
cat("1. Load the model: loaded_model <- readRDS('oahu_agriculture_rf_model.rds')\n")
cat("2. Make predictions: predictions <- predict(loaded_model, new_data[, predictors])\n")
cat("3. Predictors needed:", paste(predictors, collapse = ", "), "\n")

cat("\n=== MODEL TRAINING COMPLETE! ===\n")
cat("Your Random Forest model is ready to use for Oahu agriculture classification.\n")
```
